# Decisions

[Spec home](README.md)

Every decision in the v1 specification, in one place. This is the list we argue over.

## How to use this

- **Recommended**: my answer, waiting for your yes.
- **Agreed**: you said yes.
- **Changed**: you wanted something different, the spec file was edited, and the change log below says what it was before. A changed decision is agreed in its new form.
- **Agreed (delegated)** and **Changed (delegated)**: a technical decision. On November 12 you handed approval of these to me as technical lead. I reviewed them (see "Technical sign-off" below). You can reopen any of them at any time. One product default carries the same mark because you left it to me by name: A-13 (November 13).
- **Needs your answer**: I did not simply do what you said, or your answer raised a new question.
- **Decided for you**: you were away and told me on November 13: "stop stalling by asking me questions… come up with the answers and if you need me to approve later I will". I answered as lead, the build goes ahead on it, and it waits for your yes in the table "Decided for you, waiting for your yes" below. Name the ID to change one. This never covers spending your money, anything on the live sites or with real people's data, anything sent in your name, or a legal sign-off.
- **Open**: a call that has not been made yet. **Later**: deliberately not part of the first stages. **Dropped** and **Closed**: no longer a decision.
- To disagree, name the ID and say what you want instead.

## Where we stand (November 12, 2026)

Three rounds are done. You answered the "start here" list and most of the product files, delegated the technical files, answered the remaining real choices, and accepted the list of defaults with changes.

- **Stage 1 can start.** Every decision it depends on is settled (listed further down).
- Of 310 decisions: 114 are settled by you, 167 are settled by delegation, 8 are waiting for your answer, and 21 are later, open, dropped or closed.
- The biggest changes from your answers: Faraj first, with a TCSAAL demo at the end of Al-Hadi's season; the demo is the whole TCSAAL league; no single-team sites; no published prices; classic email and password; signed in with no time limit; reminders 24 hours ahead; group chats inside the product; league rules that drive the tracker, with a running-clock switch at the table; each team chooses who sees its players' statistics; a "Faraj test" season before the real league moves; no outside engineer for now.

## Decided for you, waiting for your yes

Answered by me as lead on November 13 to 16, 2026, because you said not to stop for questions. Every answer is the one I had recommended (S-28 to S-32 are the choices the tracker's builder made, which I accepted; F-12 to F-16 are how the Al-Hadi transfer, step 2.58, treats what it cannot bring over as it is; S-34 to S-40 answer the questions of the audit of scoring a game live, step 2.107, and of step 2.33's review; U-14, R-23, O-12, S-41, A-15, B-14 and B-15 answer the questions under the steps the audit of nothing left out, step 2.105, proposed; R-24 to R-27 answer the questions the review of step 2.126, who sees players' names, raised; S-44 and S-45 answer the questions the review of step 2.117, players at the scorer's table, raised; S-46 to S-49 and R-29 to R-31 answer the questions of the audit of using it, step 2.106, and S-50, S-51 and A-16 are answers its proposed steps rest on; A-17, A-18, S-60 to S-62 and R-32 answer the questions of the area 3 lead's walk of the staff screens on November 16, and S-63 one that step 2.93 part 3 raised). The build goes ahead on them; say the ID to change one.

The engine has no switch that ends with the last minutes, so a scorer who turns the running clock On and then Off inside them, in a game that was on a running clock before those taps, leaves it on a stop clock afterwards. Until the engine learns that (step 2.252), the scoring screen SAYS SO, in visible words, at the moment it happens and while it is so: 'The clock now stops on fouls for the rest of the game. Tap Running clock to change it back.' Where the game was already on a stop clock (a stop-clock season, or Off chosen before the last minutes), Off only puts back the clock it had and nothing is said. Nothing is locked and nothing is hidden.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | The choice that leaves the scorer the most room and is easiest to change                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

| Accessibility, languages, old phones                 | T9 sections 6 to 8                                                                |
| Cost                                                 | T1 section 8; T8 section 10                                                       |
| The founder being unavailable                        | T8 section 12 (T-166)                                                             |

### PostgreSQL or Firebase?

PostgreSQL on Supabase. The reasoning is in [T1](technical/T1-stack-and-architecture.md) section 3. In short: Supabase already gives us what makes Firebase convenient. Security is not easier in Firebase, only different, and its usual failure (a browser reading the database through a mistaken rule) cannot happen in our design, because browsers never reach the database. And PostgreSQL can refuse bad data by itself where Firebase's database cannot.

## The full list

Each line is the decision's opening sentence. The reasoning and detail are in the linked file.

The rules fixed are the season's with the given format in their place; marking the game not started empties `format` and keeps `given_format`; a trigger refuses a change to it once the game has started                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Agreed (delegated) |         |
| T-376 | An archived season is the season state that already meant over and still shown, completed: no new state and no migration (step 2.130)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Agreed (delegated) |         |
| T-377 | A write into an archived season is refused with season-archived by one check in the command framework, after the permission check and before the work; each writing command names its module check (games, teams, scheduling, leagues archived-season.ts). Entering a result and the tracker work pass only while a correction is open on the game (T-381). Also refused: division edits, order and restore, a setting written at the season (the league and a program stay open), restoring its team or game from the bin, and starting, applying, recording or undoing an import into it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Agreed (delegated) |         |
| T-378 | Start a new season copies from the program current season its rules document and statistics and its divisions (not its season-level settings: only the settings commands write a setting, record 065); teams (keeping their lineage, not those in the bin or that left) and rosters (players still on them, not in the bin, numbers kept, no joining date) only by the one choice. Registration form and site are not per season yet, so nothing of them is copied                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Agreed (delegated) |         |
| T-380 | Put the sheet back as it was (games.put_sheet_back) is not refused in an archived season: it is an admin's correction with a reason (S-7, it writes its own), as games.reopen_game is, so O-12 allows it; its own rule (sheet-put-back-rule.ts) still answers                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Agreed (delegated) |         |
| T-381 | In an archived season a game takes a result, a box score, a forfeit and the tracker's work only while a correction is open on it: its newest correction reopened it and it is not decided again since. A game corrected before archiving is no exception, and once decided again it is read-only again. A tracked game's reopen there is refused for a scorekeeper and open to whoever may correct games, with a reason. The reads that offer a button say season-archived: own reopen, the tracker's reopen for a scorekeeper, the game's rules, and the scoring offers leave out its games but those with an open correction                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Agreed (delegated) |         |
| T-387 | Standings in an archived season (O-12): an adjustment, an award and an overturn always carry a reason, so they are an admin's correction with a reason and pass; a rebuild changes no fact and passes; a coin flip passes only with its note, and taking an adjustment or a coin flip off only with its reason, else each is refused season-archived. The flip's note and the removals' reason are optional elsewhere, so the one rule is: in an archived season a standings change needs its reason. The lead confirmed this against O-12 at step 2.130's review: a standings change with a reason is an admin's correction with a reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Agreed (delegated) |         |
| T-388 | Archiving a hidden season: leagues.archive_season, and leagues.update_season asked to make it archived, refuse a hidden (draft) season with season-hidden: archived is a shown state, and an archived season can no longer be hidden, so archiving one would show it to visitors with no way back. Show it first, or leave it hidden. No other path changes whether visitors see a season but showing and hiding it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Agreed (delegated) |         |
| T-389 | Who may use an open correction in an archived season (O-12): While a correction is open on a game in an archived season, entering its result, its box score, a forfeit, the tracker's commands and the scoring session's commands are accepted only from someone who holds games.correct at the game's place; anyone else, a scorekeeper included, is refused season-archived. The archived-season check is given who acts for this, and the pages offer scoring there by the same one rule (Admin → Games, Enter the score): no one else is offered the score. A correction left open before archiving stays the correcting admin's to finish; there is no way to abandon one yet                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Agreed (delegated) |         |

| T-490 | The job queue's owner, and what each start accepts (step 2.112, record 053, T-257, T-60). **Who owns what.** Migration 0031 makes the role `queue_owner` (no login, no powers) and the empty schema `pgboss` owned by it, open to nobody else (`public` has no right there); it grants `queue_owner` to no login. pg-boss's tables are owned by the worker's login, because PostgreSQL gives a table to the login that makes it and pg-boss does not switch role. The worker's login holds `app_user` and `queue_owner` (a plain `grant queue_owner to <worker login>`), nothing else; the website's login holds `app_user` only. The migrations' catalog does not count `pgboss` among the migrations' schemas: the migrations leave it empty and what is in it is pg-boss's. **The website** (`checkLoginRole`, which judges every login as the website's unless the caller says `worker`): every rule of T-60 and the fence as before, a table it or a role it reaches owns in any schema, `pgboss` included, refused; a membership of `queue_owner`, direct or through any other role and whatever its options, refused in plain words with a revoke that cuts the way at the website's end, at the first role on it the website does not need, so the worker's login keeps its own `queue_owner` (T-496); any right on the schema `pgboss` or on a table, sequence or function in it that PostgreSQL says the login or a role it reaches HAS (has_schema_privilege and its kin, which count every predefined role: T-491), refused, each mended as the database's owner can run it (`revoke all on schema pgboss from <holders> cascade` as `queue_owner`, a table's right revoked as its owner, the owner granting itself the role for that one statement as 0031 does); a membership the holder's own grants hang on is revoked with `cascade`, for any role (T-496); `pgboss` is not a library schema for it, and the fence leaves the queue's schema to that check. **The worker** (`checkLoginRole` with `worker`, then on a hosted database `checkQueueSchema`): every rule of T-60 and the fence as before, but a table in `pgboss` owned by the login itself or by `queue_owner` is not counted as owned; a table it or any role it reaches owns in any other schema is refused exactly as before, so a worker holding `app_user` and `queue_owner` starts, and starts again after pg-boss made its tables. In `pgboss` an ordinary table without a league column that the worker may read is let be (T-482's rule, now for the worker only); a view, materialized view or foreign table there is refused, a table with a league column must have its row-level security on and forced like any league table. Since the review a table with a league column there is refused for the worker whoever owns it, mended by moving it out to the migrations' owner with its rows kept (T-493), in one `do` statement, and the next start says to ask the lead, never to drop it (T-497). **Nothing hangs on the migrations' relations (T-495).** Both starts refuse a foreign key from a relation no migration made to one they made (a table in `pgboss` included), a REFERENCES or TRIGGER right on a relation they made held by anyone but its owner, and a USAGE or CREATE right on a schema they made held by `queue_owner` or a role only the worker's login reaches; and the fence follows foreign keys' actions (cascade, set null, set default) from every relation the login may change, to any depth, and reviews the definer triggers on what it reaches. `checkQueueSchema` refuses a missing schema, a schema owned by another role (`grant queue_owner to current_user with set true; alter schema pgboss owner to queue_owner; revoke queue_owner from current_user`, which the owner can run) and a login that may not use it or make tables in it (`grant queue_owner to <login>`). **What a start does not catch (the limit).** For the worker it cannot tell pg-boss's own table from a copy table without a league column put into `pgboss` by someone holding the worker's login, `queue_owner` or the database owner's key; the worker could read such a copy, the website cannot. The columns of pg-boss's tables are not compared with pg-boss's, and triggers and rules on them are not compared with pg-boss's (a security-definer trigger function on a table the website may change, or on one a foreign key's action reaches from it, is reviewed, T-492, T-495). A foreign key among pg-boss's own tables, or from a table no migration made to another no migration made, is not refused: only one onto what the migrations made is (T-495). A league column under another name than `league_id` is not seen as one. Neither login may hold a predefined role (T-491), so the rights the checks read are the grants and memberships themselves. A grant made while the website or worker runs is seen only at its next start. As T4 says, it catches a change or drift made by hand, not a person holding an owner's key who means harm. **One login for both (proved on the real PostgreSQL, builder 2).** The two checks together refuse one login used for both services: the website's start refuses the worker's login (it holds `queue_owner`) and the worker's start refuses the website's (it may not use `pgboss`: `grant it queue_owner`); nothing else proves the two logins differ, and nothing needs to. The website's login holds `app_user` and `sign_in_store` (record 052). Where the website is judged with a login that reads pg-boss's tables, no sentence says to drop one: a table in `pgboss` is mended by `revoke select`, beside the queue sentence that names the real fault (found on the real server: before, it said `drop table pgboss.job`). **The tables' owner keeps ADMIN of `queue_owner`.** On PostgreSQL 16 a role's maker is always given ADMIN of it, without INHERIT or SET, granted by the server itself; 0031's own grant (SET, no INHERIT) is revoked, so the owner cannot act as `queue_owner` but could grant it to itself or a login. That is the owner's key, which the guard does not defend against; it is also what lets the owner grant `queue_owner` to the worker's login when a hosted database is set up. | Agreed (delegated)  |         |
| T-491 | The checks ask PostgreSQL what a login CAN do (step 2.112's review, T-490, T-60). **Predefined roles.** Neither the website's login nor the worker's may be a member, at any depth and whatever the membership's options, of a role PostgreSQL made (its name begins `pg_`): each known one is listed in `predefined-roles.ts` with why (`pg_read_all_data` and `pg_write_all_data` read or write every table, the job queue's included; `pg_read_server_files`, `pg_write_server_files` and `pg_execute_server_program` reach the server's files and programs; `pg_monitor` and `pg_read_all_stats` read every session's queries; the rest each widen reach in a way listed there), and a `pg_` role not listed (a later PostgreSQL's) is refused until it is read. Only the first predefined role on a way is named, with `revoke <role> from <the role that holds it>`; while one is held the queue's and the fence's checks are not asked, since every right they read would come through it. **Effective rights on the queue.** The website's check asks `has_schema_privilege`, `has_table_privilege`, `has_any_column_privilege`, `has_sequence_privilege` and `has_function_privilege` for the login and every role it reaches (a superuser aside, named as one already), not the schema's grant list alone: any right on `pgboss`, or on a table, view, sequence or function in it, is refused. A function there counts when a reached role is granted it by name or when it is a security definer: every function may be run by everyone unless revoked, and pg-boss's own are no definers and sit in a schema the website may not use. **Mendings the owner can run.** A grant made by `queue_owner` or by an object's owner is revoked as that role: the owner grants itself the role with SET for that one statement and takes it back, as 0031 does; a membership of `queue_owner` whose holder made grants of it is revoked with `cascade`; the schema is given back to `queue_owner` in three statements. Each is run as printed by the owner on the real PostgreSQL in `tests/real-postgres/queue-review.test.ts`; the predefined roles only on PGlite, since the owner there may not grant them. Guarded saves of one league take turns with each other; the league's other writes are not blocked, because a row that only points at the league (an activity row, say) takes a key-share lock that FOR NO KEY UPDATE does not conflict with, where FOR UPDATE would hold up every such insert and could deadlock with an admin's setting change. The league row is always the first lock these saves take, so they cannot wait on each other in turn. Without it, a yes given while child A was recorded could outlive A put in the bin while child B was added, if B's save read the league before the bin committed. A league row that cannot be held stops the save. No migration. Proven by unit tests that each command asks for the lock before it reads (calls written down in order), by a database test beside the query that requires `for no key update` and the league filter in what it sends (it fails with the clause taken out), and by the database tests on PGlite, which has one connection. Reasoned and not run: two connections at once, that is the saves really waiting on each other and an insert of the same league not waiting. | Agreed (delegated)  |         |

| T-321 | What the device keeps of the tracker belongs to the account that made it. The tracker page carries `<meta name="srleagues-account" content="{account id}">` (also on its refusals); the worker shows a kept page only while the network says that account is signed in, or does not answer within three seconds (with no signal the device is still the maker's: signing in needs the network); when a late answer then names another account or nobody, the kept pages are deleted and the page is opened again from the network. When the network says another account or nobody (sent to sign in, refused as signed out, a page that names no account), every kept page of another account is deleted and never shown. A kept page that names no account is never shown. Each play in the queue keeps `accountId`; a game's queue is sent, listed in "Your games" and dismissed only for its maker, so another account's plays stay on the device for their own account and the signed-in one sees none of them. Plays stored before the maker was kept are listed for whoever is signed in. The store of opened games already let go of another account's games on opening (`stillKept`). Rules: `accountMarkOfPage`, `signedInFrom`, `mayServeKeptPage` (tracker-worker-rules.ts), `madeBy` (queue-storage.ts).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Agreed (delegated) |         |
| T-322 | The update rule of T-127 and T-319, made exact (the lead's decision, step 2.38 part 4): a game holds a new release back only while it is open as a scorekeeper means it: it is not final, or plays of it still wait on this device to be sent. A final game with nothing waiting holds nothing back, nor does a game the device has let go (no longer in its store of opened games), whatever of it waits. When the store cannot be read, a release waits; when only the queue cannot be read, every kept game counts. Before this a release waited while the store held any game at all, which in practice meant until signing out or the 14-day clean-up. Rule: `gamesHoldingBack` (tracker-worker-rules.ts), read by the worker from the opened games store and the queue. Also (step 2.38 part 4, T-253): a device whose own session ended while it was away and which is given a new one sends the taps still waiting under the old one under the new one when nobody else scored since the state it last knew; otherwise they are listed as not saved.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Agreed (delegated) |         |
| T-327 | What a device keeps belongs to one person (the lead's decision, step 2.38 fix round, review M1). Every kept page, kept game and kept play carries the id of the person it was kept for. The device holds a mark of who is signed in here (an id, no secret: `device-account.ts`), written by every signed-in page load that reaches the network (pages with the account's sign-out form; the tracker page once the server answers its opening) and so by signing in, deleted by signing out. With no network a kept page or kept game is shown only when its owner is the marked one, otherwise the plain offline page. When another person's id replaces the mark, the earlier person's kept pages and games are forgotten (the worker's forget path); their unsent plays stay on the device, hidden, and are sent only when that person signs in here again. A batch of version 2 says whose plays it carries (`accountId`): the client never sends another person's plays, and the server refuses a batch whose stated maker is not the account of its session (the session decides; the stated maker can only refuse). Plays kept before this release name nobody: never sent, listed to nobody. Before this, with no signal a kept page opened for whoever held the device.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Agreed (delegated) |         |

When the server answers "update needed", Reload tells each worker to delete its kept pages and files and a waiting worker takes over, so the reload opens the new release from the network; the plays waiting on the device are in its own storage, survive, and the new release sends them. Nobody can be held on a refused version. Replaces T-322's count of stored games, which could hold a release back for the 14-day keep.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Agreed (delegated) |         |

| T-330 | The tracker's rosters and changes of players on the device (step 2.118). A change of players (add, several numbers in one line, renumber, rename, take off) goes through the controller like a tap: timed by the server's time, checked against the contract and against the server's own rules (S-37, S-45) before anything is stored, every change of one line checked before any is stored, stored before it is listed, refused when the device is not scoring, listed as not saved on a loss, in the one queue with the person who made it (T-327). The device fetches the rosters on opening, on taking over, after a loss, after a refused change and when back online, and keeps each. The list is always the kept rosters with this device's waiting changes on top; a change the server took is laid on the kept rosters until a fetch begun after it answers. With no answer on opening the device starts from the rosters it kept before this opening, not the page's copy. An add whose answer was lost is checked against the fetched rosters before it is called not saved, and one found there leaves the list and the storage. The Players panel (part 2) draws that list and decides nothing: each player's marks and rules come from the device's rules file and every change goes through the controller. What is typed in it is kept in the browser's own storage by game, so a half-typed line survives the panel shut and a reload; losing that storage loses only typing. On an upright phone, while starters are picked, each team takes half of the teams' place and scrolls by itself, so seventeen a side never pushes the second team under the pad.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Agreed (delegated) |         |

The game shown is rebuilt from the storage read in that lock, so a tap stored but not yet laid on the game is counted once; a tap made meanwhile under the session that ended is judged like the others (moved and sent if nobody else scored, listed otherwise), never left waiting unsent; and from then on taps are made under the new session. | T-336 | The takeover question's facts (S-42, step 2.148). A game is under way when the server's game is live, which a reopened game is again; a lapsed holder of a game under way is never displaced by an opening, which is answered `held-by-other`, and only a confirmed takeover naming that holder's `since` takes it (logged as any takeover). A game not yet live is still simply opened once its holder lapsed. The holder's `lastHeardAt` is when its lease was last written, so up to about half a minute early (T-295), never before its session began; `sameAccount: true` is set by the server when the holder is the asking account on another device, never told by names. Both are optional in the reply's schema so a tracker reads an older server; a tracker opened before this release fails to read a reply carrying them, so a release should not fall during a takeover (T-127 covers commands, not this reply)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Agreed (delegated) |         |

Every other 404 from a league endpoint, the gate's `not-found` (a hidden or missing league, or a scorer signed out in a draft league), is read by the tracker (`asksSignIn` in `tracker-controller.ts`) as "sign in again" with every waiting tap held, exactly as a 401; an uploaded copy's page reads it as signed out too. A tracker opened before this reads `unknown-game` as no answer and keeps asking, so it drops nothing. Likewise the invitation's Accept button (`turnedBackTo` in `apps/web/src/features/access-area`) sends a visitor at a hidden league, and a signed-in person holding no invitation for it, to the platform's home, where a missing league sends them, so the two cannot be told apart                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Agreed (delegated) |         |
| T-456 | A scorer is never told "sign in" for ever (step 2.223, completing T-453; the lead's decision). When a league endpoint answers 404 without `unknown-game`, the tracker asks one question about no league: `GET /api/v1/signed-in` answers `{ "signedIn": true or false }` (`SignedInAnswer` in `packages/contracts`; `signed-in-endpoint.ts`), reading no league and no access, so it tells nobody anything about a league. Signed out, or no answer: as T-453, sign-in asked, every tap held. Signed in: the tracker turns read-only for the reason `cannot-open`; the screen says this account can no longer open the game and that every tap not yet saved is kept on this device, and offers "Save a copy" (step 2.70) to hand them to the league's admin. It never loops (asked one at a time, and read-only stops the renewals), never sends the person to a page that answers 404, and never drops or sets aside a tap. Nothing is added under `/api/v1/leagues`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Agreed (delegated) |         |

Then (part 2) step 2.194's walk runs from one shared function, `tests/browser/first-test-walk.mjs`, which its browser test also calls; the league (short name, name, season, draft or not) and the owner's sign-in are its parameters. The rehearsal's owner signs in on the sign-in page with the password chosen at sign-up and shows the season `league:make` left hidden; the league is a draft, so the owner reads steps 16 to 18 and the visitor, signed out in a second browser, must get 404 on each of those pages. Then `npm run check:test-copy` with the build's own `--manifest`, every line passing. `--expect-refusal=certificate` (no `PLATFORM_DATABASE_CA`) and `--expect-refusal=confirm-email` (the fake with `mailerAutoconfirm`) pass only when the website's start prints its own refusal sentence, matched to startup.ts's words, and fail when it starts | Agreed (delegated) |         |
| T-302 | `scripts/check-test-copy.mjs <address>` checks a test copy from outside, read-only and with no secret: it reads no environment, takes https or plain http to this computer only (localhost, 127.0.0.1) with nothing after the address, follows a redirect only on the same host (5 at most), and waits at most 10 seconds for each answer. It sends GET requests and one POST, the "be this person" form for a person no copy has, to `/signin/made-up-people` and to `/signin/no-such-page`. "Do not index" is the `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` header and the page's own mark on the front page, the sign-in page, a made-up league's address and a page that does not exist, and the header with "every robot, nowhere" on `robots.txt`. "Exactly as `/signin/no-such-page`" is the same status and the same body once three things are put in one place: the page's one-time script nonce (read from the answer's own policy), the address's last name, and the order of the streamed data pieces; headers are not compared, as a host's proxies add their own to every answer. The action's id is new at every build, so it is given (`--action-id`, or `--manifest` with the build's `server-reference-manifest.json`); without it that line fails as not checked. Against a hosted copy nobody outside can know that id, so `--without-action` prints that one line as NOT CHECKED, with the reason, in the summary too, and it fails nothing: the rehearsal on this computer (`npm run rehearse:test-copy`), on the same code with the build's manifest, is what proves the posted action. Exit code 0 only when no line failed, 1 when one failed, 2 when it refused                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Agreed (delegated) |         |
| T-448 | Since step 2.90 a team's page in Admin → Teams finds a person for its roster on the server: "Find a person by name" sends the browser to the team's own address with `?q=` (a name only, never an email, which never rides in an address, T-76: for an email the address holds only `?find=by-name` and the page says in words that people are found by name), and the league list is read by core's `people.list_people` in this league only, by name and public name, 200 to a page with `?page=` (a plain whole number, anything else is page 1), the search and page kept through an add or a refused add with scripts on or off, so a league of any size can pick anyone (`teams-area/person-pick.ts`, the one place of that rule). "Not on the league list" and "Put back" read the list as whole only when nothing is searched and the first page holds it all
